labels.name: module:parser
labels.description: Anything associated to the parser module.

issue.body:
## Problem:
While running social_smell_showcase.Rmd on the Apache Thrift github repository (https://github.com/apache/thrift), on line 139

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L139

I got the following error:

Error in data.table::setnames(perceval_parsed, "data.body", "reply_body") : 
  Items of 'old' not found in column names: [data.body]. Consider skip_absent=TRUE.

### Steps I took to try and fix it:
-Checked my perceval_path and mbox_path and made sure they were correct and relative to my working directory
-Checked my perceval installation & tried different installation methods
-Used a different mbox file. First I tried the one provided for the Apache Thrift project by Rick. Then, I used the mbox here https://lists.apache.org/list.html?dev@thrift.apache.org.
-Tried running the notebook on another project. In particular, I tried to run the notebook for the Apache Helix github repo (https://github.com/apache/helix), but that didn't seem to make a difference. 

### My findings:
I looked at the source of the parse_mbox() function in parser.R, and I tried to learn more about the error.

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/R/parser.R#L243-L281)

One thing I noticed was that if I set stderr=TRUE in line 250-253 of this function

  perceval_output <- system2(perceval_path,
                             args = c('mbox',mbox_uri,mbox_path,'--json-line'),
                             stdout = TRUE,
                             stderr = TRUE) # set to true

Then I get the following error message:

Error: parse error: after array element, I expect ',' or ']'
                                 [2023-01-26 22:19:07,492] - Sir Perce
                     (right here) ------^

I know the "[2023-01-26 22:19:07,492]" seems to refer to the time I ran the notebook. I believe "Sir Perce" refers to perceval, but I don't understand why perceval is giving this error.

Also if I set verbose=TRUE in line 255 of this function:

line 255)   perceval_parsed <- data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(perceval_output),verbose=TRUE)) # changed verbose to TRUE

The console output says "Imported 0 records.  Simplifying...".

So perceval_parsed is an empty table, which I believe explains why I was getting this error from before:

Error in data.table::setnames(perceval_parsed, "data.body", "reply_body") : 
  Items of 'old' not found in column names: [data.body]. Consider skip_absent=TRUE.

Referencing this documentation for the setnames() function, https://rdrr.io/rforge/CALIBERdatamanage/man/setnames.html, I see that "old" represents the old columns of the dataframe, and since the dataframe was empty, "old" wasn't found.

The problem I have is I don't understand why perceval_parsed ends up being empty.

### To replicate error:
-clone Kaiaulu and install Kaiaulu package
-clone Apache Thrift repo (https://github.com/apache/thrift)
-set up the project configuration file for thrift.yml following the example here (https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/conf/helix.yml). Specifically, I just set up the version control and mailing list section
-Within, social_smell_showcase.Rmd, change tools_path and conf_path (here: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L58-L59)
-run the social smells notebook

issue.title: How to edit identity tables manually on Social Smells notebook?

labels.name: module:identity
labels.description: For changes associated to the identity matching module

issue.body:
Hi Jari,

I'm moving your question here since it may be of use to others and to make it easy to refer to code lines.

@tuejari 
> I was editing the reply_from column when the warnings appeared, not the column raw_name. So I was wondering whether you were using the correct column in the rest of the code. To my understanding, you add the columns identity_id  and raw_name with the identity matching, but it doesn’t seem to be the case that you use these columns in other parts of the code (or at least not for the mbox files).

I got some time to revisit the code to refresh my memory. Here how it works:

1) First, we specify in the social smells notebook which column the person's name (and/or) e-mail is:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L168-L172

Above, `author_name_email` and `reply_from` are the specified columns, for GitHub and Mailing List respectively. Perhaps the flexibility of this function is misleading, as the `transform_` functions used after will assume you did so. 

2) For example, when the git log is transformed into bipartite in the social smells notebook:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L267-L268

The function expects `author_name_email` to contain the column:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/R/network.R#L18

The same is true for the mailing list `transform` function, which was recently generalized to `reply` to accommodate issue comments from JIRA, GitHub, and Pull Request comments:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/R/network.R#L277-L283

All the `transform_` functions encode assumptions on the table, but they all rely on `model_direct_graph()`, which is in `graph.R`, which only reason graphs. 

3) Therefore, to answer the original question, if you want to manually edit the identity table, the column you should care about are `author_name_email` and `reply_from`. But you also have to remove the additional row you manually decided to be the same identity. For example, suppose row 5 states that three names and emails are from person A, and row 9 states 2 names and emails are from person B. Then, you can update row 5 with row 9 information, and then delete row 9 or vice-versa. 

You will want to ensure for every identity pair you do that, you do so consistently on both `project_gitlog` and `project_mbox`.

Please let me know if you think this is not working as described above.

milestone.title: 0.0.0.9500 Standardized API data columns
milestone.description: Different data sources call the same thing different things. The codebase originally did not have overlap, but currently the overlap leads to lack of clarity. Some functions also evolved: For example, parse_*_network() now has an alternative function parse_*_temporal_network(). Therefore parse_*_network() should be renamed to parse_*_bipartite_network() or renamed altogether. See #43.

issue.body:
Now that newer data sources and tools are available in Kaiaulu, the project configuration file sections are becoming more confusing. There is also little comment guidance on what is needed or not, or what is part of Kaiaulu or what is not. 

The overall format should be refactored to facilitate understand its purpose, where to obtain the field values and what uses them. 

Fundamentally, these files take inspiration from Codeface, but go a bit further. The goal is to "distill" a project's website available infrastructure information, and therefore data, in a concise, reusable file that can be manually checked and reused for other analysis. For instance, here is a list of questions that often wastes manual time to be answered for every analyzed project:

 1.  Version Control:
    1. What version control system is used? Git, SVN, something else? 
    2. Where is the data for analysis X? 
 2. Mailing List: 
    1. What mailing list archives the project use? (e.g. pipermail, mod_mbox, MARC, google groups, etc)
       1. Do they contain the same data? (OpenSSL is a classic example where each archive contains a portion of the full mailing list!)  
    2. What mailing list should be used for analysis? Developer and User, or just developer? Any other mailing list?
    3. What is the URL for the mailing lists we should use?
    4. Where is the data for analysis X? 
 3. Issue Tracker
    1. What issue tracker type is used (BugZilla, JIRA, GitHub, TRAC, etc)
    2. Where is the data for analysis X?
4. Files 
    1. What language does the project use? (Needed as a parameter for static analysis tools, and to avoid including non src code files in your churn metrics!)
    2. How do developers convention test files? (Need to also avoid bloating churn and other content metrics)
    3. Do commit messages contain conventions for issues or software vulnerabilities? (Needed for bug count metric, or software vulnerability analysis). 
  
These questions all require some manual time is spent googling the project website to find (which is not even always easy to locate), manual inspection of commit messages to curate a regular expression, etc. A project configuration file should make it easier for a person to quickly assess that, and more importantly, stop wasting time searching for it. This information is of course not immutable: An analysis of OpenSSL over its entire 20 years lifespan shown it started with mailing lists, overlapped with a bug tracker and mailing list, and eventually moved fully to GitHub. So some minimal validation the links in the files are current, or sufficient for the analysis of interest, is still important.

Of course, the information in this file can be capitalized by Kaiaulu to do something: Knowing the online source of a VCS, Mailing list or issue tracker can be used by a crawler to obtain the data, whereas the local path can be used to execute the pipeline in the R Notebooks, and eventually via a command-line interface.

# Analysis 

From here, the second concern is reproducibility in MSR and the analysis, which is often buried in online folders, or e-mails. For example, was only a portion of the project X mailing list used? What was the time window? What commits range was used in the git log? Or what types of file dependencies were used? These parameters are per analysis, but missing one of them dooms any future attempt to effectively compare results. These parameters have to nonetheless be decided so an analysis can occur, and deferred to the user instead of hardcoded and buried under functions, which is unlikely to be found on normal usage of the tool. Further thought on whether embed this on a project configuration file or R Notebook directly is still needed.

issue.title: Identity Matching Smells Notebook - Warnings
issue.body:
In https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/126#issuecomment-913052673, @carlosparadis states regarding the implementations of community smells that "the textual names are mapped to a temporary id within function scope at this step." 

In the social smells notebook, in the section on Identity Matching

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L159-L179

The following is stated:

> You may also manually correct the identity numbers, before executing the remaining code blocks, to improve the accuracy of the results.

So, since the social smells implementation uses the textual names, the textual names also need to be manually corrected. 

After trying to manually fix some mistakes in the identity matching, I got the following warnings from this part of the social smells notebook: 

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L193-L356

```
Warning in if (clust != neigh_membership) { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
Warning in matrix(unlist(extra.clust.links), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) :
  data length [637] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of rows [319]
```

Note that the first warning is repeated a lot of times, and the second warning occurs occasionally in between. 

I am using the following command to change the name in `project_mbox`:

```{r}
project_mbox[<index>]$reply_from <- ‘<new-name>’
```
So for example:
```{r}
project_mbox[20:25]$reply_from <- ‘Firstname Lastname <f.lastname@example.com>’
```

(Note that I also manually change the `identity_id`, but that is not causing issues, likely because it is not used.)

I have tried to fix the identities right after 

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L159-L179

@carlosparadis mentioned the following potential problems:
> You may be editing the incorrect column in the table. Assuming you are doing this after the identity match is executed, I believe there should be two columns: id, and name added to it. The id is as I said, the numerical identity. the name column on the other hand collapses all the various name a person had and put them in a single string separated by "|". 

The warnings occur when I change the `reply_from` column in `project_mbox`. If I do not change the `reply_from` column, but instead change the `raw_name` column, I do not get warnings anymore. So it may simply be the first case, that I edited the incorrect column in the table. However, it could also be the case that the column `raw_name` is not used correctly.

Assuming that the warnings arise from the cluster algorithm, 

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L285-L298

I noticed the following. When `network_mbox_slice` is created, the column `reply_from` is used, not the column `raw_name`:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/5a003899207fd55980a9d9df1c5584e339854508/R/network.R#L272-L284

@carlosparadis also mentioned another potential problem:
> Another potential problem is that you may be creating duplicates by re-assigning (in fact I'd wage this as a strong candidate to be the issue). There should only be one row for each identity, your error suggesting a vector of size > 2 in later portions of the code may be due to duplicates. 

However, I am not sure that I understand this correctly. Each identity can occur multiple times in `project_mbox`, repeated for each mail they sent in the mailing list. I have checked and I do not introduce duplicate rows in the data table, if that is what you meant. I simply alter the values in specific cells.  

@carlosparadis mentioned the following:
> If the code runs just fine before you try to make manual changes, and this is a simple value replacement, then the value assignment is likely the culprit. Either due to the wrong column, or the wrong assignment. This variable is at the end of the day just a table. 

The code does run just fine before I make any manual changes, so I do expect the value assignment to be the culprit. Specifically, when I change the column `reply_from`.
